Journalist and author Bob Woodward, whose reporting took down former President Richard Nixon, believes history will remember President Donald Trump’s transgressions as more consequential than those committed by Nixon.

Appearing on “The Axios Show” this week to promote his new memoir, Woodward held nothing back when asked about Trump, noting the current president’s level of corruption surpasses that of Nixon, who resigned from office in 1974 amid the Watergate scandal.

“Trump is worse — much worse than Nixon,” he said. “He’s made billions of dollars himself as president. … It used to be a scandal if the president was getting a free ride on somebody’s jet. Now he gets a free jet!”

As for what Americans will most “remember and endure” with regard to Trump’s presidency in the future, Woodward believes it will be the ongoing Iran war.

Presidents, he said, “are known for their wars, but in this case, it’s such a mistake. It’s a mistake for Trump to use that power to launch a war against a country. We shouldn’t start wars. We should prevent wars.”

Woodward, 83, rose to prominence as a reporter for The Washington Post in the early 1970s. His reporting for the Post ― much of which was produced in collaboration with fellow journalist Carl Bernstein ― broke the news of the Watergate scandal that led to Nixon’s resignation and helped his outlet win a Pulitzer Prize in 1973.

In the 53 years since then, Woodward has written or co-written 24 books on U.S. politics, including four detailed accounts of George W. Bush’s presidency.

So far, he’s written another four books that are focused heavily on Trump. His experiences with the current president also feature prominently in “Secrets: A Reporter’s Memoir,” released this week.

When asked if there’s anything he admires about Trump, Woodward offered the president some faint praise that doubled as criticism.

“He persists; he doesn’t give up,” he said. “And we’re now in a situation where he’ll do anything to stay in power.”

“President Nixon had people who were in his circle who tried to stop wars and prevent wars,” he continued. “In Trump’s circle now, there are all these people who are just feeding the beast. He’s the beast, and he’s being fed with kind of, ‘Oh, it’s OK to start wars.’”
